turns.content: Hello, my car has broken down and I cannot repair it, so I need to buy another one quickly. I have found a used vehicle at 12 000 € and I would like to know how I can finance this purchase, given that I would need the funds within two weeks.

To replace your vehicle, the suitable financing is the **Expresso Auto Loan**: it is the offer dedicated to buying a used vehicle, with a more advantageous APR than a conventional personal loan.

On the 12 000 € amount, here is what an indicative simulation gives (excluding optional insurance, 0 € application fee):

- **Over 48 months**: indicative APR of 5.49% → monthly payment of around **279 €**, total cost ≈ 13 400 €, i.e. ≈ 1 400 € of interest.
- **Over 60 months**: indicative APR of 6.29% → monthly payment of around **233 €**, total cost ≈ 14 000 €, i.e. ≈ 2 000 € of interest.

Extending the term eases the monthly payment but increases the total cost: that is the trade-off to make depending on the margin you want to keep.

On affordability, your situation is sound: your current debt-to-income ratio is 20% and your monthly savings capacity around 928 €. A monthly payment of 279 € therefore remains manageable, even if it would reduce your monthly savings. Point to watch: your current account balance is low (1 517 €) and your available savings (14 695 €) could usefully reduce the amount borrowed if you wish — without that being an obligation.

On the schedule, this is the point to monitor: the fund release timeframe for this offer is at least **8 working days**, which is compatible with a fortnight, but without much margin. I would advise starting the application quickly.

The simulation above is indicative and non-contractual: only the signed loan agreement and subscription are binding. For the firm offer and the final pricing, the simplest route is the official simulator:

[URL|Simulate and subscribe to the Expresso Auto Loan|https://particuliers.sg.fr/emprunter/credit-auto-deux-roues/credit-auto-expresso]

If you would prefer to be guided, you can also book an appointment or request a callback:

[URL|Book an appointment with an advisor|https://particuliers.sg.fr/vos-rendez-vous]
[RAPPEL|Request a callback from an advisor]
Thank you for these details. I have 14 695 € of savings: is it worth using part of it to reduce the amount borrowed, or is it better to keep this savings aside?

Using part of your savings is the most effective lever here, for a simple reason: every euro of savings used is a euro you do not borrow, and therefore a euro on which you pay no interest.

In practice, on your 12 000 € project, here is what a down payment changes, for information (excluding optional insurance, 0 € application fee):

- **No down payment**: 12 000 € borrowed over 48 months → monthly payment ≈ 279 €, total cost ≈ 13 400 €.
- **With a 4 000 € down payment**: 8 000 € borrowed over 48 months → monthly payment ≈ 186 €, total cost ≈ 8 930 €, i.e. around 930 € of interest instead of 1 400 €.

You therefore save several hundred euros of interest and significantly ease your monthly payment.

That said, you should not empty your reserve: your current account balance is low and your savings are your safety cushion. The ideal is to use only part — for example 3 000 to 4 000 € — keeping the rest available for the unexpected.

On affordability: your situation remains sound in both cases. Your current debt-to-income ratio is 20% and your monthly savings capacity around 928 €, so even the monthly payment without a down payment remains manageable. With a down payment, you also keep more comfortable day-to-day room for manoeuvre. The point to monitor remains your day-to-day cash position, which is tight.

These figures are indicative and non-contractual: only the signed loan agreement and subscription are binding. To decide precisely on the amount of your down payment and obtain the firm offer, the official simulator lets you test each scenario:

[URL|Simulate and subscribe to the Expresso Auto Loan|https://particuliers.sg.fr/emprunter/credit-auto-deux-roues/credit-auto-expresso]

And if you would like to discuss it, you can book an appointment or request a callback:

[URL|Book an appointment with an advisor|https://particuliers.sg.fr/vos-rendez-vous]
[RAPPEL|Request a callback from an advisor]
Understood, so I will keep part of my savings and put in around 4 000 € as a down payment. Concretely, how do I start the application and make sure I have the funds within two weeks?

With a 4 000 € down payment, the amount to borrow drops to 8 000 €. Over 48 months, the applicable rate for this amount is 5.49%: the monthly payment comes out at around **186 €** and the total cost of the loan at around **8 930 €**, i.e. approximately 930 € of interest. This scenario is consistent with your savings capacity and your current debt-to-income ratio, so it is sustainable.

To start the application, everything is done online from the offer page: you enter the amount (8 000 €), the term and your down payment, then you submit the case file. That is also where you will get the firm offer and the final pricing.

[URL|Simulate and subscribe to the Expresso Auto Loan|https://particuliers.sg.fr/emprunter/credit-auto-deux-roues/credit-auto-expresso]

On the timing, however, I would rather be straightforward: this offer states a fund release of at least **8 working days**. A fortnight is therefore still feasible, but the margin is thin — I cannot guarantee that the funds will be there within that timeframe, as it depends on how the file is put together and approved. If the schedule is really tight, the safest option is to speak directly to an advisor to lock in the vehicle handover date.

[URL|Book an appointment with an advisor|https://particuliers.sg.fr/vos-rendez-vous]
[RAPPEL|Request a callback from an advisor]

The pricing above remains indicative and non-contractual: only the signed loan agreement and subscription are binding.
You say the timeframe is a bit tight: if ever the funds are not available within the fortnight, is there another solution so that I can pay for the car on time?

If the schedule tightens, there is indeed a fallback solution among the offers available to you: the **Alterna Revolving Credit**. Its interesting feature here is the fund release timeframe, stated at **48 hours by transfer** — so much shorter than the 8 working days of the Expresso Auto Loan. That said, this timeframe remains an indicative order of magnitude: it depends on how the file is put together and approved, and I cannot guarantee a release on a specific date.

The point to know before turning to this option: it is significantly more expensive for a one-off purchase. The rate applied to the amounts used is **16.9%**, versus 5.49% for the Expresso Auto Loan on 8 000 € borrowed over 48 months. On an amount used of 8 000 €, that represents a noticeably higher cost of credit than with the dedicated offer. And since it is a revolving credit, it does not work like an amortising loan with constant instalments: interest applies to the amounts actually used, with monthly payments that depend on the amount drawn.

My recommendation therefore remains clear: **favour the Expresso Auto Loan**, which is the most economical offer for your project, and only switch to Alterna if the 8 working days really cannot be met. In that case, it is better to talk to an advisor to decide between the two and lock in the vehicle handover date.

On affordability, your situation remains sound: with a current debt-to-income ratio of 20% and a monthly savings capacity of around 928 €, either solution remains manageable — the real issue here is cost, not your repayment capacity.

The figures above are indicative and non-contractual: only the signed loan agreement and subscription are binding.

[URL|Simulate and subscribe to the Expresso Auto Loan|https://particuliers.sg.fr/emprunter/credit-auto-deux-roues/credit-auto-expresso]

Thank you, that is clear. If I go for the Expresso Auto Loan and really want to secure the vehicle handover date, can I book an appointment with an advisor right now to arrange all of that?

Yes, that is the right approach to secure the vehicle handover date: the appointment allows you to lock in the schedule with the advisor and to start assembling the file without delay.

Two things concretely determine whether the two-week timeframe is met:

- **Completeness of the file**: the earlier the supporting documents (identity, income, proof of vehicle purchase) are gathered, the faster validation can proceed.
- **The order of the steps**: start the financing application first, before firmly setting the handover date with the seller — that is what leaves you room if processing takes a few extra days.

On affordability, the project remains comfortable: with your current debt-to-income ratio of 20% and a monthly payment of around 186 € on 8 000 € borrowed, the effort remains manageable given your monthly savings capacity.

Perfect, I will book an appointment and start the application online. Just one last thing: do I need to bring any particular documents to the appointment so that the file moves faster?

Good question, and this is exactly the kind of detail that saves days.

I cannot give you the exact list of documents: it is not documented in the information I have, and it depends on your file. What really moves things forward, however, is arriving at the appointment with the documents already gathered rather than sending them afterwards. The advisor will confirm the precise list to provide, but prepare the essentials now: your identity and proof of address documents, your recent proof of income, and the items relating to the vehicle (the seller's listing or order form).

One practical point: ask for this list when you book the appointment, so you can put it together before the date. That, together with approval of the file, is what really determines whether the two-week timeframe is met.

On affordability, nothing changes: with a monthly payment of around 186 € on 8 000 € borrowed, the effort remains manageable given your current debt-to-income ratio.
